title: bee-chain-nudge + bee-state-sync hooks incl. worktree-holds renewal, conformance
action: Port the two heavy hooks whose dependencies are now all in Rust, onto the rust-port-7 hook runtime: (1) bee-chain-nudge — SubagentStop advisory JSON (worker-collect nudge when a bee worker or swarming phase, review-synthesis nudge, scribing-debt warning) built on the already-ported state/cells readers; silent when nothing applies. (2) bee-state-sync — throttled heartbeat touch, reservation lease renewal, cross-worktree hold renewal (port the remaining worktree-holds renewal path), and the locked rebuildStateProjection call from rust-port-16 with LOCK_BUSY skipping silently (msn-7 F8: never writes workflow records); completely silent, always exit 0. RIG NOTE (the rig is NOT a shared module): the conformance discipline lives duplicated in-file — copy the seeded-root, sha256-oracle-verification, node-verdict-non-triviality, twin-pairing and negative-control helpers from crates/queen-bee/tests/hook_conformance.rs (the rig of record), exactly as crates/queen-bee/tests/modelguard_conformance.rs did. Build ONE target heavyhooks_conformance: advisory-text parity for chain-nudge across its trigger classes and silence classes; for state-sync, side-effect parity — the state.json rebuild result, heartbeat/lease/hold renewals, and the LOCK_BUSY skip — plus crash fail-open on both.

truths: cargo --test heavyhooks_conformance runs and reports at least 12 passed, fixture names listed per class
chain-nudge advisory JSON matches node byte-for-byte across trigger classes, and both runtimes stay silent on the silence classes
state-sync side effects (state.json rebuild, heartbeat, lease and hold renewals) match node on the same fixtures; LOCK_BUSY skips silently on both
crash fixtures exit 0 with a hooks.jsonl crash line on both runtimes

artifacts.substantive: chain-nudge and state-sync hooks plus heavyhooks_conformance corpus

key_links: rig helpers copied from crates/queen-bee/tests/hook_conformance.rs (no shared test module exists)
rig drives the real bee-chain-nudge.mjs and bee-state-sync.mjs as sha256-verified oracles
state-sync uses rust-port-16 rebuildStateProjection under the D9 lock
prohibitions: No wiring-file edits — ported hooks stay dark until the flip slice
state-sync never writes workflow records (msn-7 F8)
Tests never touch the live .bee/ store
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml members list

trace.outcome: Ported bee-chain-nudge (advisory SubagentStop nudge, read-only) and bee-state-sync (silent state-projection/heartbeat/lease/hold refresh) onto queen-bee's hook runtime, plus the write paths bee-core needed to back state-sync: claims::heartbeat_session/renew_claim_ttl, reservations::renew_holds_by_session, holds::renew_holds (cross-worktree). heavyhooks_conformance.rs (16 tests) proves byte-identical advisory JSON / silence across trigger classes for chain-nudge, and side-effect parity (state.json rebuild, heartbeat, claim/lease/hold renewal, LOCK_BUSY skip, crash fail-open) for state-sync against the real frozen mjs oracles.
deviations: 1. Scoped ports, not full mjs API surfaces. The cell's action calls for
heartbeat touch, reservation lease renewal, and cross-worktree hold
renewal — but claims.mjs, reservations.mjs/lease-store.mjs, and
worktree-holds.mjs each expose a much larger mutating API (session
create/adopt/release/sweep, epoch fencing, lease acquire/release,
mirrorHold/releaseHolds/sweepExpiredHolds). Only the ONE write path each
module's hook call site actually exercises was ported:
`claims::heartbeat_session`/`renew_claim_ttl` (never `presentedEpoch`
fencing, adoption, or lane binding), `reservations::renew_holds_by_session`
(never lease acquire/release), `holds::renew_holds` (never
mirror/release/sweep). Every unported function stays exactly as it was
(CLI-only, out of this cell's scope) — documented at each new function's
own doc comment.
2. Byte-compatibility bug self-caught by this cell's own oracle diff, fixed
before capping: the first `heartbeat_session`/`renew_claim_ttl` draft
round-tripped the on-disk record through bee-core's typed `Session`/
`Claim` structs (`read_session(...).last_heartbeat = ...;
write_json_atomic(...)`). Those structs name `lane`/`transcript_path`
(Session) and `session`/`claimed_at`/`ttl_seconds` (Claim) as
`Option<...>` WITHOUT `skip_serializing_if`, so a typed round-trip always
emits the key — `null` when the source record omits it. The mjs source
never does this (`session.last_heartbeat = ...; writeJsonAtomic(file,
session)` on the plain object `readSession` returned, which only ever has
the keys the file already had). `heavyhooks_conformance.rs`'s
`state_sync_heartbeat_claim_lease_hold_renewal_matches_oracle` caught the
divergence directly (rust session.json grew `"lane": null,
"transcript_path": null` the node oracle's never did). Fixed by patching
the raw `serde_json::Value` in place for both writes instead of the typed
round-trip — the typed `Session`/`Claim` readers stay as they were
(read-only call sites are unaffected; only these two NEW write paths
changed). `holds::renew_holds`'s `Hold` round-trip was checked against
the same risk and found safe: `worktree-holds.mjs`'s `insertHold` always
writes every field explicitly (nulls included, never omitted), so a
typed round-trip there introduces nothing new.
3. `chain_nudge.rs`/`state_sync.rs` use each hook's OWN root variable
exactly as the mjs source does, not a uniform "always pass control root"
rule: `bee-chain-nudge.mjs` never references `ctx.controlRoot` at all
(every call — `hookEnabled`, `readState`, `resolvePipeline`,
`scribingDebt` — takes the bare hook root), while `bee-state-sync.mjs`
mixes both (`heartbeatTouch`/cross-worktree `renewHolds` take the
control root; `renewHoldsBySession`/`rebuildStateProjection` take the
bare root and re-derive control-root internally in mjs). This port
follows the established rust-port-16 pattern of a caller-supplied,
already-resolved control-root parameter rather than re-deriving it
inside bee-core, matching each call site's literal mjs identifier usage.
